title: Hira gasy troupe contest
summary: Hira gasy is a day-long performance of the Malagasy highlands: a village troupe gives speeches, harmony songs and dances before its neighbours, often in a contest with another troupe that the crowd judges by its cheers.
howToPlay: You are the young speaker of a village troupe on a market plaza.
Tap a choice, or press its number, to decide what you do at each part of the show.
When a saying needs its last word, pick the one you think is right; your line is written on the song page.
Wit and harmony grow as you choose well; your ending gives one to three stars.
rules: The show follows the old order: drums, speech, song, dance and a closing piece.
Patient, generous and clever choices earn wisdom points; boasting and mocking earn none.
Bragging, mocking another performer or shaming a singer cannot be undone and costs the best ending.
Each saying is answered once; a wrong answer costs a little wit or harmony.
Three stars need wit and harmony and none of those missteps.
heritageNote: Hira gasy comes from the central highlands of Madagascar, where troupes of related families, in matching jackets and dresses, travel to perform at gatherings and markets. The speeches, songs and dances follow a set order and carry advice about living well together. This is an original contest story in that spirit.
